title: upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + ROPE fused ops + scheduler/kv-cache tweaks
author: Sofia Nguyen
description: Motivation: Reduce tail latency and improve throughput for medium/long sequences across our hosted and dedicated fleets by upgrading attention kernels and applying a set of micro-optimizations. This PR upgrades our attention implementation to FlashAttentionV2 where applicable, introduces a fused ROPE/rotary op to avoid extra kernel launches and memory traffic, and applies scheduler and KV-cache integration tweaks to keep throughput gains under realistic traffic patterns. Changes are gated behind a runtime feature flag (ATTN_USE_FLASHV2) and can be disabled per-deployment. Summary of changes: - Introduce FlashAttentionV2 CUDA kernels and integrated build plumbing for supported SM versions. - Add fused ROPE/rotary kernel that applies positional encoding in the attention path with reduced transposes and memory copies. - Add a small fused split/concat path used for QKV layouts that reduces launch overhead for small batch sizes. - Scheduler changes: better sequence-length bucketing when continuous batching is enabled; dynamic kernel-selection policy based on sequence length and KV-cache hit rate. - KV cache: reduce copy-on-read by exposing zero-copy view paths for cached key/value tensors; adjust cache eviction heuristics to prefer shorter sequences when under memory pressure. - Tests/benchmarks: microbenchmarks (CPU/GPU) and integration e2e perf tests added; CI includes a new bench job for safety. Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout -> internal canary on dedicated cluster -> gradual rollout to hosted tenants with shadow testing. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] microbenchmarks added [x] smoke/end-to-end validated on dedicated canary [x] feature flag + config documented [x] perf regression guardrails added

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Nice work here — can you add a comment explaining the heuristic constants in the bucketing logic? There's a magic '1.2' factor in batch_coordinator.rs.
Author (Sofia Nguyen): Added explanatory comments and moved the factor into a named const (BUCKET_COST_FACTOR). PTAL.
Priya Sharma: On ROPE fused kernel: did you measure register pressure at seq_len=2048? The tmp register count looked high in the profiler sample.
Author: Yup — profiled on A100 and found increased register usage; I added a fallback codepath that emits the unfused ROPE when register pressure > threshold and added an autotune flag.
Luca Rossi: KV-cache zero-copy looks good but ensure it's disabled for older CUDA drivers where pinned memory semantics differ.
Author: Guarded the zero-copy path behind driver version check and added a runtime warning to logs when falling back.
CI system: bench/attn failed on first run due to flaky rng seed; rerun passed and results attached.
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 and introduced a fused ROPE kernel. Expected improvement: 15-25% throughput on long sequences and 10-18% lower p95 latency for seq=512/1024 on our A100 fleet. Rollout behind feature flag. No API changes.
summary_metrics: Throughput: +22% seq=1024 (A100 40GB) on typical prompt mix
P95 latency: -18% seq=512 under continuous batching workloads
KV-cache hit path: +8% effective throughput when hit rate > 60%
Scheduler: 7% lower variance in batch formation time (reduced outliers)
notes: Feature flag: ATTN_USE_FLASHV2 defaults to false for older clusters.
Canary: tested on dedicated-canary-3 for 48 hours before wider rollout.
Backports: nominated for backport to release/2026-02 branch (cherry-pick prepared).
